# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto proposes reducing employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, abolishing self-employed National Insurance entirely, and introducing "Triple Lock Plus" for pensioners to ensure State Pensions and tax-free allowances rise annually. The party commits to no increases in income tax, VAT, or corporation tax, while maintaining fiscal rules requiring public debt to fall and borrowing to stay below 3% of GDP.

## Taxation and Families

Child Benefit changes would move to a household-based system, with reductions beginning at £120,000 combined income. Working parents would receive 30 hours free weekly childcare from nine months old until school age. A Family Hub would be established in every local authority.

## Immigration

A legally binding annual cap on migration would be introduced, with parliament voting on levels each year. The Rwanda deportation scheme would continue with regular flights. Asylum processing would be completed within six months, ending hotel accommodation use.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would reach 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in UK munitions production. A National Service scheme would require 18-year-olds to choose between military placements or civic volunteering.

## Healthcare

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 more doctors recruited. Plans include 50 new Community Diagnostic Centres, modernising 250 GP surgeries, and expanding pharmacy services.

## Housing

The target is 1.6 million homes in England, with permanent Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. Green Belt protections remain, with development focused on brownfield sites.

## Energy and Environment

Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing would continue. Nuclear power expansion includes two new Small Modular Reactor fleets. Green levies on household bills would be reduced. Net zero by 2050 remains the target.

## Transport

£36 billion from cancelled HS2 Phase 2 would fund local transport projects, including £8.3 billion for road maintenance. The £2 bus fare cap would continue throughout the parliament.

## Education

The Advanced British Standard would replace A-levels and T-levels for 16-19 education. 100,000 additional apprenticeships would be funded by closing underperforming university courses. Mobile phones would be banned in schools.
